t.1.19.2: My lotus-eyed Rāma is not yet sixteen years old; I do not see in him any fitness for battle with the rākṣasas.
t.1.19.1: O tiger among kings, having heard those words spoken by Viśvāmitra, he remained for a moment as though senseless; then, regaining consciousness, he said this.
t.1.19.4: These servants of mine are heroic and valorous, skilled in weapons, and fit to fight the hosts of Rākṣasas; you should not take Rāma.
t.1.19.3: Here is a full akṣauhiṇī, of which I am the lord and master; surrounded by it, I shall go and fight with those night-roamers myself.
t.1.19.5: I myself, bow in hand, will be your protector at the forefront of battle; as long as I hold on to my life, so long will I fight with the night-roamers.
t.1.19.6: That excellent vow of yours will be well protected and free from obstacles. I myself will go there; you ought not to take Rāma.
t.1.19.7: For he is a boy, his training is not yet complete, and he does not know what is strong and what is weak; he is not endowed with the power of divine weapons, nor is he skilled in battle. He is no match for the rākṣasas, for they surely fight by deceit.
t.1.19.8: For, separated from Rāma, I cannot bear to live even for a moment, O tiger among sages; you ought not to take Rāma away.
t.1.19.9: Or if, O brahman of good vows, you wish to take Rāghava, then take him with me, accompanied by an army of four divisions.
t.1.19.10: Sixty thousand years have passed since I was born, O Kauśika, and this son was begotten with great hardship; you ought not to take Rāma away.
t.1.19.11: Indeed, among my four sons my love is greatest for him; you should not take away Rāma, the eldest, who holds dharma as foremost.
t.1.19.13: And how, O Brahman, are those rākṣasas who fight by treachery to be countered by Rāma, or by my own forces, or by me?
t.1.19.12: Of what valor are those rākṣasas, whose sons are they, and who are they? Of what stature are they, and who protects them, O bull among sages?
t.1.19.14: Tell me everything, O blessed one: how am I to stand against those evil-minded ones in battle? For the Rākṣasas are swollen with pride in their might.
t.1.19.15: Having heard those words of his, Viśvāmitra spoke: "There is a rākṣasa named Rāvaṇa, born of the lineage of Paulastya."
t.1.19.16: He, having been granted a boon by Brahmā, sorely oppresses the three worlds; of great strength and great valour, he is surrounded by many Rākṣasas.
t.1.19.17: It is heard that there is Rāvaṇa, the lord of the Rākṣasas, of great valor, the very brother of Vaiśravaṇa and son of the sage Viśravas.
t.1.19.19: Thus addressed by that sage, the king then said to the sage: "Indeed, I am not able to stand in battle against that evil-souled one."
t.1.19.18: When that mighty one, Rāvaṇa, does not himself obstruct the sacrifice, then, urged on by him, those two exceedingly mighty rākṣasas, Mārīca and Subāhu, will obstruct the sacrifice.
t.1.19.20: Therefore, O knower of dharma, grant your favour to my dear little son. The Devas, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, birds and serpents…
t.1.19.22: And I am not able to fight against him or against his forces, O best of sages, whether with my army or together with my sons.
t.1.19.23: O Brahmin, by no means will I give up my son, my dear little boy, godlike in appearance though he is, a mere child unskilled in battles.
t.1.19.21: They are not able to withstand Rāvaṇa in battle, how much less mere men? For in battle that rākṣasa takes away the valor of the valorous.
t.1.19.24: Moreover, if those two, the sons of Sunda and Upasunda, who are like Death in battle, are the ones who obstruct your sacrifice, I will never give you my little son.
t.1.19.25: Mārīca and Subāhu are both mighty and well trained. With one or the other of those two I would do battle myself, together with my band of allies.
